triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The household-level SSN and student screens were satisfied whenever at least one member passed (count_where(member_of_household, snap_member_ssn_requirement_eligible) > 0), a fail-open aggregation that let a household with SSN-ineligible or student-ineligible members clear the gate, whereas the member predicates (7 CFR 273.6, 273.5) make the household test 'no member is ineligible'.
triage.triage_notes: This file is module.kind: composition (assembled rather than encoder-generated), so a reviewer may prefer not_a_rule_module; it is format: rulespec/v1 and its rules carry real formulas, so I kept it as a rule module. Three formulas changed meaning: snap_ssn_eligible and snap_student_eligible flip from count_where(..._eligible) > 0 to count_where(..._ineligible) == 0, and snap_work_requirement_eligible drops its 'count_where(..._eligible) > 0 and' conjunct (which fail-closed a household where no member was affirmatively work-eligible, e.g. all exempt). I confirmed on main that us/regulations/7-cfr/273/6.yaml defines snap_member_ssn_requirement_eligible as 'not snap_member_ssn_requirement_ineligible', so the pre-fix formula resolved fine and was simply wrong logic, not a dangling reference. The snap_eligible change (snap_income_eligible -> (snap_income_limit_exemption_for_categorically_eligible_household or snap_standard_income_eligible)) is semantically neutral: it just follows the rename/narrowing in index 2, where the old snap_income_eligible was exactly that disjunction. The commit also ADDS five rules (member_of_household data_relation, snap_gross_monthly_income, snap_monthly_household_income, ny_snap_excess_shelter_cost, snap_excess_shelter_deduction, snap_initial_month_allotment_after_minimum_issuance) plus proof-atom metadata on every rule; that added wiring is new coverage, not a defect fix. Note the fix is incomplete: snap_residency_citizenship_eligible still uses count_where(..., snap_member_citizenship_or_alien_status_eligible) > 0, the same fail-open pattern. The proof atoms for all these composition rules cite us/guidance/usda/fns/snap-fy2026-cola/page-1 (the FY2026 COLA memo), which says nothing about SSN/student/work screens, so the 'cited source' anchor for this module is weak; the defect is nonetheless a real inversion relative to the federal member-level rules it composes. The pre-existing companion test ssn_ineligible_household_gets_zero_allotment uses a one-member household and passes under both formulas, so the defect was invisible to the module's tests.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as composition wiring or a forced rename and could not: both `snap_member_ssn_requirement_eligible` and `snap_member_ssn_requirement_ineligible` exist as sibling rules in the imported `us/regulations/7-cfr/273/6.yaml` (with `snap_member_ssn_requirement_eligible: formula: not snap_member_ssn_requirement_ineligible`), and the same eligible/ineligible pair exists in `273/5.yaml` for students, so the edit was a free choice of aggregation semantics, not a repair of a dangling reference. The pre-fix household screens passed whenever any one member cleared the member predicate (`count_where(..., *_eligible) > 0`), i.e. fail-open, while 7 CFR 273.6(a) read through the pinned corpus requires "the social security number (SSN) of each household member or apply for one before certification" — so the flip to `count_where(..., *_ineligible) == 0` changes encoded meaning in exactly the fail-open→fail-closed direction the first reader described. The companion change to `snap_work_requirement_eligible` drops a redundant-but-fail-closed `count_where(..., *_eligible) > 0` conjunct, which is the same boolean-combination family. This is a formula change, not proof-hash or metadata bookkeeping (those are present in the same diff but are not what the reader cited), so mechanical and not_a_defect both fail.

triage.verifier_notes: Evidence checked: diff 000.diff; pre/post of policies/otda/snap/fy-2026-benefit-calculation.yaml at 29d5044 and a495db3292; imported member predicates in us/regulations/7-cfr/273/6.yaml (lines 25-44), 273/5.yaml (lines 267-284), 273/24.yaml (lines 330-346); 7 CFR 273.6 text via resolve_provision (corpus release us-sc-snap-2026-07-15, provision sha 0520761c903c...). Caveats a reviewer should weigh: (1) the commit is a 4-bullet squash — most of the diff is composition glue (new member_of_household data_relation, snap_gross_monthly_income, snap_monthly_household_income, ny_snap_excess_shelter_cost, snap_excess_shelter_deduction, snap_initial_month_allotment_after_minimum_issuance) plus proof-atom metadata, which is mechanical/additive; only the four Judgment formulas carry the defect. (2) The snap_eligible change (`snap_income_eligible` → `(snap_income_limit_exemption_for_categorically_eligible_household or snap_standard_income_eligible)`) is a mixed case: `snap_income_eligible` does not exist as a rule anywhere under us/regulations/7-cfr, us/statutes/7 or us/policies at HEAD, so part of it is a dangling-reference repair, and the added disjunct is closer to unrepresented_clause (categorical eligibility exemption from income limits) than to polarity. If the corpus wants one kind per case, polarity_or_logic still dominates (2 of 4 rules are pure fail-open flips, a 3rd is a conjunct removal). (3) The post-fix household screen is itself stricter than 273.6(c) — "The disqualification applies to the individual for whom the SSN is not provided and not to the entire household" — so the fix is directionally correct against 273.6(a) but the composition still lacks per-member exclusion; that is a separate, unfixed gap, not a reason to reject this case. (4) No companion test exercises the multi-member fail-open path: the `ssn_ineligible_household_gets_zero_allotment` case uses household_size 1, where both the pre and post formulas yield not_holds.
